meta.title: Right-to-work boilerplate that is not a refusal

payload.requisition_text:
Software Engineer — Integrations
Duncastle Tech Ltd · Soho, London

Duncastle connects UK restaurant tech: POS to delivery platforms to accounting. 3,000 venues run their order flow through our integrations.

You'd own connectors end to end in a Node/TypeScript estate: new platform integrations, version migrations, and the conformance suite that keeps partners honest.

Requirements
- 1-3 years of backend experience
- Evidence you've debugged an integration you didn't write
- All applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

£41,500 · 25 days holiday · hybrid (2 days Soho) · annual conference budget. Interview: portfolio chat, then a paired debugging session on a real (sanitised) incident.

expected.determining_fact: The right-to-work line is standard boilerplate that neither offers nor refuses sponsorship — sponsorship itself confers the right to work, so the sentence does not settle the employer's stance.

evidence_anchors.willingness_quote: All applicants must have the right to work in the UK

design_notes: The boilerplate trap pointed at false NOT_SPONSORABLE: a naive reading treats the right-to-work line as a refusal and discards a role at a licensed sponsor. Ground truth is boilerplate_ambiguous, not silent — the topic is touched but not settled — which changes only the report's advice line.
